title: Regional ejection from delayed telemetry leading to fallback amplification — incident retrospective
creator: Anita Kapoor
description:
Summary: On 2025-10-28 at ~09:12 UTC, a telemetry ingestion lag in the regional aggregator caused stale health signals to be propagated to the control plane. The control plane interpreted the stale metrics as a sustained regional failure and ejected an EU region pool from routing. The ejection caused a sudden reroute of persistent sessions and long-running KV-cache-backed token streams to other regions. Those regions then began hitting per-tier capacity limits and automatic fallback policies activated, cascading into an amplified fallback surge to lower-capacity model variants and increased end-to-end latency for customers across multiple accounts.

This ticket is the incident retrospective describing what happened, the immediate mitigations we executed, root cause analysis, and the remediation plan to prevent recurrence.
timeline: 2025-10-28T09:12Z - Alerts: control-plane emitted 'region-unhealthy' for eu-west-2. Initial alert volume increased due to route error spikes seen in API gateways.

2025-10-28T09:16Z - Ops: on-call investigated dashboards; regional health metrics (heartbeat_rate, avg_inflight) showed drop but telemetry ingestion lag suspected after cross-check with node heartbeats.
2025-10-28T09:23Z - Mitigation: manually disabled automatic regional-ejection policy for eu-west-2 to stop further large-scale drain triggers.
2025-10-28T09:35Z - Mitigation: rolled back recent change to telemetry sampling in the aggregator (PR #4862) and restarted aggregator workers in eu-west-2 to restore fresh signals.
2025-10-28T10:05Z - Stabilization: routing drift subsided; traffic began to rebalance; fallback activations reduced but tail latency remained elevated for 30–45 minutes.
2025-10-29T11:00Z - Post-incident: started RCA with telemetry, control-plane, and serving runtime leads.
root_cause: A deployment that changed telemetry sampling and batching in the regional aggregator (intended to reduce ingestion cost) introduced a windowed buffering behavior. Under the normal traffic pattern, buffered batches caused a 30–90s lag in propagation of per-node inflight and heartbeat metrics to the control plane. The control plane’s ejection heuristic treated the stale low-heartbeat counts as a persistent regional failure, triggering an automated drain. The drain caused reroutes which exceeded target region and tier capacities and invoked fallback policies simultaneously across multiple routing tiers, amplifying the impact.
mitigations: Disabled automatic regional-ejection policy during incident to prevent further mass drains.
Reverted telemetry sampling change (PR #4862) and restarted aggregator workers to flush buffers and restore real-time metrics.
Applied temporary rate cap on fallback rollouts so that fallback activation is sequenced rather than simultaneous across many routes.
Opened priority ticket to increase observability for telemetry lag (dashboards and alert thresholds).
permanent_fixes: Introduce conservative staleness window: control plane will ignore ejection triggers derived from metrics older than 20s unless multiple corroborating signals exist.
Implement explicit heartbeat/heartbeat-ack path separate from aggregated telemetry so that health decisions use direct node heartbeats when available.
Add jittered rollout to fallback activations: fallback policy will now probe at low QPS and ramp based on successful probe success rate to avoid mass simultaneous fallback amplification.
Improve telemetry ingestion design: switch from larger buffered batches to micro-batching with bounded latency and backpressure guarantees.
Add an integration test that simulates telemetry lag and validates that control-plane ejection heuristics do not trigger on short-lived staleness.
follow_up_actions: (Owner: telemetry) Build micro-batching change and schedule canary in staging — due 2025-11-12.
(Owner: control-plane) Implement staleness-window gating logic and unit tests — due 2025-11-05.
(Owner: routing) Add fallback ramping feature and associated rollout dashboard — due 2025-11-20.
(Owner: observability) Create dedicated telemetry-lag dashboard and an automated runbook to triage staleness alerts — due 2025-11-07.
Run tabletop exercise simulating telemetry loss and fallback surge with on-call rotation — responsible: SRE and Eng Leads — schedule Q4 2025.
notes: We observed that customers with long-lived streaming sessions (chat with KV cache) saw the highest error amplification because stateful reroutes caused KV cache misses and degenerated request sizes.

The fallback surge primarily affected mid-tier (tier-B) model variants where capacity headroom was low; high-tier (tier-A) and low-tier (tier-C) were less impacted due to capacity and routing behaviors.
There was no evidence of malicious activity; this was an operational regression introduced by a telemetry optimization.

This incident highlights tight coupling between telemetry freshness and automated routing decisions; we must treat health signals as safety-critical and conservatively gate autonomous actions that cause mass reconfiguration.
